title: Renters' Rights Act 2026: Key Changes for Landlords and Tenants
excerpt: The Renters' Rights Act 2026 introduces significant reforms to UK renting laws, effective from May 1st. The Act notably bans no-fault evictions.
author: Reyse Radar

body.text: The Renters' Rights Act 2026 is set to bring about substantial changes in the UK housing market starting May 1st. A significant provision of this Act is the ban on no-fault evictions, altering the landscape for both landlords and tenants.

The Act, which became law in October 2025, is designed to provide greater security to tenants. The prohibition of no-fault evictions means landlords will no longer be able to terminate a tenancy without a valid reason, thereby offering tenants more stability in their housing arrangements.
Implications for Estate and Letting Agencies

For estate and letting agencies, staying compliant with the new legislation is imperative. Agencies should update their tenancy agreements to reflect these changes and ensure that all staff are informed about the new legal requirements. Additionally, agencies might consider revisiting their landlord advisory services to support clients in navigating these new regulations.

In practical terms, this means reviewing and potentially revising existing contracts to ensure they comply with the new legal standards. Agencies should also consider hosting informational sessions or creating resources for landlords to understand the implications of the new Act and how to manage their properties under these new rules.
